record.original_question: Prove Solovay’s Conjecture: there exists a constant L such that for all sufficiently large n, there are at least Q^n/2 strings s of length n satisfying K(s) ≥ |x| − L and H(s) ≤ |x| + H(string(n)) − 1/2 K^2(string(n)), where Q is the size of the underlying alphabet and H and K denote, respectively, Chaitin and Kolmogorov-Chaitin complexities.

evidence.quote: In a topological sense, ‘many’ Kolmogorov random strings are not Chaitin random. Prove Solovay’s Conjecture: There exists a constant L such that for all sufficiently large n, there are at least Qⁿ/2 strings of length n, s, such that K(s) ≥ |x| − L; and H(s) ≤ |x| + H(string(n)) − 1/2 K²(string(n)). (Here Q is the size of the underlying alphabet, H and K are, respectively, Chaitin and Kolmogorov-Chaitin complexities, cf. C. Calude, Information and Randomness, Springer, 1994.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet of size $Q \geq 2$, and let $\Sigma^*$ denote the set of finite strings over $\Sigma$. For a string $s \in \Sigma^*$, let $|s|$ denote its length. Fix a universal Turing machine and a universal prefix-free (self-delimiting) Turing machine, and define:
- $K(s)$, the plain Kolmogorov–Chaitin complexity of $s$, i.e. the length of a shortest input to the universal machine producing $s$;
- $H(s)$, the Chaitin (prefix-free) complexity of $s$, i.e. the length of a shortest input to the universal prefix-free machine producing $s$.
For a positive integer $n$, write $\mathrm{string}(n)$ for the standard string encoding of $n$ in $\Sigma^*$.

Prove or disprove the following statement (Solovay's Conjecture): there exists a constant $L$ such that for all sufficiently large $n$, the number of strings $s \in \Sigma^n$ satisfying both
$$K(s) \geq n - L \qquad \text{and} \qquad H(s) \leq n + H(\mathrm{string}(n)) - \tfrac{1}{2} K^{(2)}(\mathrm{string}(n))$$
is at least $Q^n/2$, where $K^{(2)}(x) := K(K(x))$.

In words: a positive fraction (at least one half) of the length-$n$ strings are Kolmogorov-random (up to an additive constant) but fail to be Chaitin-random by a quantitatively specified gap.
artifact.status_search_result: Solovay's observations comparing plain and prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity are well known, and related quantitative results (e.g., Bienvenu–Muchnik–Shen–Vereshchagin on maximal plain vs. prefix-free complexity) have appeared. However, available sources do not clearly confirm or refute the exact form of Solovay's conjecture as stated (with the $Q^n/2$ counting bound and the specific $H(\mathrm{string}(n)) - \tfrac12 K^{(2)}(\mathrm{string}(n))$ gap), so the precise status remains unclear from accessible literature.

status_evidence.title: Complexity of Complexity and Maximal Plain versus Prefix-Free Kolmogorov Complexity
status_evidence.snippet: Solovay showed that infinitely many strings x have maximal plain complexity but not maximal prefix-free complexity; for some c: |x| - C(x) ≤ c and |x| + K(|x|) - K(x) ≥ log_2 |x| - O(log_3 |x|).
status_evidence.claim: Related Solovay-type results comparing plain and prefix-free complexity exist, but the specific Q^n/2 conjecture is not asserted as resolved.

status_evidence.title: Kolmogorov Complexity and Solovay Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Solovay functions: computable upper bounds f for K with f(x) = K(x) + O(1) for infinitely many x.
status_evidence.claim: Solovay's name is associated with several distinct objects in algorithmic information theory; the conjecture in question is a separate counting statement whose status is not clearly settled in the surveyed literature.
